protocol: D-000 turn 3 of 3, same cycle as turns 1 and 2, last turn; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 successor replacing exact-machine pinning with a hosted-fleet-class measurement contract, plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers
summary: My SHOULD-FIX landed in full and in the form I asked for. There is now a per-platform trade table stating, for each of the four classes, what changed against D-006 and which direction it moves the bar — stricter on macOS arm64, easier in RAM headroom on both Linux rows, with the RSS consequence guarded by 'Extra RAM is not a license to grow the process'. The warrant is separated honestly rather than stretched: D-000 preference-laden product sign-off covers the four-platform set, and OBS-T3-02 is claimed only as the Intel-specific reason. The entry also stopped calling labels exact machines and replaced that with a fleet-class contract carrying all three components the prompt names. I simulated the five edits: eighteen named identifiers, one reserved cell which is G13, zero survivals of PARTLY MET, and — a detail worth crediting — zero survivals of 'fixed runner image', a phrase the fleet contract would otherwise have left false.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, Decision clause 4, first two bullets
notesNonBlocking.observation: Both bullets are introduced as replacing a 'harness-cell prefix', but each replacement also rewrites the cell's matrix description: 'cold-cache harness, p50/p95/p99, fixed runner image' becomes '… fleet class', and 'same runners and lifecycle commands' becomes 'same fleet classes and lifecycle commands'. The substance is not merely defensible but necessary — under a contract that permits weekly image rolls, leaving 'fixed runner image' in the register would have created exactly the stale-statement problem I raised against D-092, and I confirmed by simulation that the phrase drops from one occurrence to zero. Nothing is concealed either, since the fenced blocks quote both strings in full and are what an executor follows. The note is only that the clause labels understate their own scope: a later reader auditing what D-094 changed from the bullet headings alone would see 'prefix' and not learn that each gate's matrix text moved with it. Calling them cell replacements rather than prefix replacements would close the gap.

The attack 'turn-1 or turn-2 subject edited' fails: both measure unchanged at start and end, 263d2565… and e20f8535…, equal to the values this subject pins for them.

The attack 'D094-T2-SF-1 not landed (class trade or warrant missing)' fails on both limbs, and the repair is the one I proposed rather than a paraphrase. The per-platform table gives D-006's class, the new fleet class, and the effect on the same numerals for each of the four platforms, and it states the direction rather than hiding it — macOS arm64 'Smaller machine. The same ms/RSS bars are stricter. Accepted.'; both Linux rows 'Larger machine. The same bars are easier in RAM headroom. Extra RAM is not a license to grow the process. Accepted.' That last clause matters, because RAM headroom is precisely where a larger box could have quietly relaxed the RSS bars. The successor section also states the binding change in terms — the numerals 'now bind to the fleet class, not to a single host' — which is the acknowledgment I said was missing, and it carries D-006's falsifiability rule forward verbatim in substance: a bar that proves infeasible needs a successor 'with the measurement attached, never a silent waiver'.

The warrant limb is answered by widening the claim honestly rather than by asserting the narrow one covers everything: 'Warrant: D-000 PREFERENCE-LADEN product sign-off of a procurable four-platform set. OBS-T3-02 is why Intel is the GH Intel VM rather than a 2018 Mac mini. It is not claimed as the sole warrant for the arm64 or Linux re-pins.' A rejected alternative also engages the narrower option I left open — confining the successor to Intel — and gives a reason for declining it rather than ignoring it.

The attack 'ADV-D094-T2-01 not landed' fails, and all three named components of the fleet contract are present rather than gestured at. Preflight is nine items, fail-closed, with 'Any mismatch discards the sample. It is not averaged in.' Successor triggers are enumerated in both directions — documented CPU, RAM, storage or architecture change, label retirement or replacement, and OS family change require a reviewed successor; a new VM per job and a weekly image roll within the same OS family do not, provided preflight still matches, and are recorded on every sample. The cross-VM rule sets a qualification result as p50/p95/p99 over N=11 independent jobs on fresh VMs, cold and warm separately, compares release-to-release on the same fleet class, and states that 'A single-VM number is not a qualification result.' The entry also stops calling labels machines: 'Labels are not one machine and are not an immutable image digest.'

The attack 'flips condition 4 to MET without a complete fleet contract' therefore fails on the contract's completeness, and the naming arithmetic is verified by simulation rather than by reading. I applied all five edits to a copy of the live register: the result contains exactly eighteen 'named: harness.' strings, one surviving 'reserved, not named' cell which is G13 — the row this entry refuses to name — and zero occurrences of 'PARTLY MET' anywhere in the file.

Condition 4's three limbs still hold on the turn-3 text, resting on the verification I did at turn 1 from D-001's own wording, 'Required release gates have named harnesses and owners; no document claims QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED without retained evidence.' The naming half reaches 18 of 18 by simulation, owners are untouched at 22 of 22 with G03 and G04 both owned by Release engineering, and the claims half is unchanged, with no gate row asserting QUALIFIED and every DEMONSTRATED occurrence in file 08 an abstinence statement or the requirement text.

All five targets are unique and the two landing in the same table row are disjoint, as established at turn 1: the three fenced targets each occur once and their replacements zero times, and '| **PARTLY MET** |' and 'condition 4 is PARTLY MET' each occur exactly once.

The supersession of D-006 is scoped, stated, and reversible, which is what makes it lawful rather than a quiet amendment. The entry says it 'supersedes D-006's exact-machine / exact-OS requirement for G03 and G04 only', gives the reason — hosted runners are new VMs per job with weekly image rolls, so they are not one machine — preserves the numerals and the regress-only 10% rule, and the reversibility clause restores 'D-006's pre-successor exact-machine requirement and runner class'. D-006 is itself PREFERENCE-LADEN route C, so a same-class scoped successor under dual review is the mechanism available.

The lifting of the v3 reservation is reasoned rather than assumed. gate-harness-naming.v3 reserved G03/G04 until a D-006-conforming successor pinned machines, OS versions, cache-state protocol, product sign-off and Intel procurability, or a successor routed unprocurability. This entry redefines what a pin is for these two gates and then satisfies the redefined requirement, and it says so in a rejected alternative — 'the D-086 reservation was for missing pins; the fleet-class contract is the successor pin' — rather than treating the reservation as silently discharged.

The attack 'silent Rosetta or Apple-Silicon-hosted Intel' fails on the same surfaces as turn 2, with the conservative check preserved: value 1 rejects, value 0 accepts only with independent native-Intel host and process facts, ENOENT accepts only on those same facts, any other error rejects, closing 'Never measure Intel on Apple Silicon. Never Rosetta.'

The attack 'changes D-006 numeric threshold numerals' fails: the header, the successor section, the trade table and a rejected alternative all preserve them, and the deliberate exclusion of analyze RSS and doctor-with-consented-probes RSS is carried forward.

The attacks 'presents 16 of 18 after naming, or 18 of 16', 'claims QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED', 'marks any DR row SATISFIED' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/ or flips condition 5' all fail: the replacement reads '18 of 18', both inserted cells end 'not authored; not QUALIFIED', clause 3 states 'MET is not QUALIFIED. MET does not authorize implementation', clause 5 refuses SATISFIED and the implementation directory, and condition 5 stays last with condition 2 at 4 of 30 NOT MET.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on every row: COORD 4ec06988…, file 08 45dc4611… and the freeze all equal live bytes at start and close; the three commits resolve at full hash to D-086, D-088 and D-093; and all four reviewer-verdict pins match — my own at 2dcb0d20… and fcfe3b25…, and the two Codex files at 76a3dc34… and 940b336b…, both hashed without opening.

I considered it and did not raise it: at that sample size those percentiles collapse toward the maximum observation, which makes the gate stricter rather than laxer, so the choice errs safe and is within the product sign-off this entry carries.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Across three turns this entry moved from a pin whose procurability evidence described a different machine, to a pin that was the venue but re-pinned every platform without saying what that did to the thresholds, to this: a fleet-class contract that admits labels are not machines, and a table that states per platform which way the bar moved and accepts it in both directions. That last part is what I asked for, and the phrase 'Extra RAM is not a license to grow the process' does the specific work of stopping a bigger Linux box from quietly loosening the RSS bars. The warrant was widened honestly rather than stretched, and the alternative I had left open — confining the successor to Intel — is engaged and answered rather than ignored. One detail deserves credit beyond my own findings: the replacements delete 'fixed runner image' from the register, which under a contract permitting weekly rolls would have become false, and that is the D-092 staleness failure caught before a reviewer had to raise it. My single note is that the clause headings call these prefix replacements when they also rewrite each gate's matrix text; the fenced blocks are exact, so this is labeling, not substance.
